title: Surface-visible deliverables: publish, scope, and lifecycle rules
summary: How mission/task-session artifacts reach the deliverable inbox and mission-asset surface intact across tenants and archive.
hint_triggers: Rules learned while making mission deliverables visible on surfaces: (1) publish with a tenant for tenant missions — an ArtifactRecord or inbox entry without tenant_slug is org-shared, visible only at public tier, and invisible to every tenant-scoped outcome feed; (2) deck-kind records need metadata.slides_count at publish or the DELIVERABLE_QUALITY finish gate blocks the mission; (3) deliverables must be promoted to a durable floor before the archive move — report/export records re-point to the tenant or system artifact floor, so they survive finish; (4) persist repo-relative paths — machine-absolute paths in the shared inbox store embed host layout and die on other machines; (5) mission ids are not tenants — any code that derives a tenant from missions/<tier>/<seg>/ must validate the segment with isValidTenantSlug; (6) write volatile faces with the caller-resolved missionDir — volatile() fallback lands in the unqualified layout and materializes a shadowing skeleton.
